title: Nagpur Civic Body Approves Rs 240 Crore Road Resurfacing Project
body: The Nagpur Municipal Corporation on Tuesday approved a Rs 240 crore road resurfacing project covering 85 kilometres of arterial roads across the city, officials said. The project, expected to begin next month, will prioritise stretches in Dharampeth, Sadar, and Manish Nagar that have seen repeated complaints of potholes during the monsoon season. Municipal Commissioner Abhijit Rao said the resurfacing work will use a polymer-modified bitumen mix intended to withstand heavier rainfall than the previous surface. Contractors have been given an eight-month completion window, with a two-year maintenance warranty built into the tender. Opposition corporators raised concerns during the general body meeting about the timeline given similar projects in the past that ran over schedule. The civic body has assured that traffic diversions will be announced in phases to minimise disruption. Work on the first phase covering Dharampeth is expected to start by the third week of next month.

title: Vidarbha Records Above-Average Monsoon Rainfall, IMD Issues Orange Alert
body: The India Meteorological Department has issued an orange alert for Nagpur and surrounding Vidarbha districts, forecasting heavy to very heavy rainfall over the next 48 hours. Regional weather officials said the region has already recorded 18 percent above-average rainfall this monsoon season, with several low-lying areas in the city experiencing waterlogging over the past week. The Nag River, which flows through the city, is being monitored closely after water levels rose sharply following heavy overnight showers on Sunday. District authorities have advised residents in flood-prone areas near Ambazari and Gorewada to remain alert. Schools in three talukas were shut on Monday as a precautionary measure. The IMD said conditions are expected to ease from Thursday as the monsoon trough shifts northward, though isolated heavy spells cannot be ruled out through the rest of the week.

title: Vidarbha Cricket Association Announces Squad for Ranji Trophy Season
body: The Vidarbha Cricket Association on Wednesday announced its 18-member squad for the upcoming Ranji Trophy season, retaining the core group that reached the quarterfinals last year. The squad will be led by veteran batsman Faiz Fazal, with young pace bowler Yash Thakur named vice-captain following a strong domestic season. Selectors said they were particularly pleased with the depth in the pace bowling attack, adding that conditions at the Vidarbha Cricket Association Stadium in Jamtha typically favour seam bowling early in the season. The team's first match is scheduled against Madhya Pradesh next month at home. Head coach Sanjay Ramaswamy said the focus during the pre-season camp has been on building fitness levels and adapting to the newly relaid outfield at the stadium. Vidarbha finished as runners-up in the tournament two seasons ago and will be aiming to go one step further this year.

title: Orange City Ganesh Festival Committee Unveils Theme for This Year's Celebrations
body: The Orange City Ganesh Utsav Committee has announced that this year's central pandal theme will focus on water conservation, tying into the civic body's ongoing rainwater harvesting drive. Committee organisers said the pandal, expected to be set up near Sitabuldi, will feature an interactive exhibit on the city's groundwater levels alongside the traditional idol installation. Organisers confirmed that immersion this year will be restricted to designated artificial ponds at five locations across the city, continuing a policy introduced three years ago to reduce pollution in natural water bodies. The festival committee has also tied up with local schools for an eco-friendly idol-making workshop ahead of the festival. Last year's celebrations drew an estimated 400,000 visitors to the central pandal over the ten-day period, according to committee estimates. Preparations for this year's event are expected to begin in earnest next month.

title: Nagpur University Announces Revised Exam Schedule After Student Union Representations
body: Rashtrasant Tukadoji Maharaj Nagpur University has announced a revised examination schedule for undergraduate final-year students following representations from the student union over an overlap with placement season. The revised dates push the examination window back by two weeks, university officials confirmed on Monday. Vice-Chancellor Dr. Prashant Bokare said the decision was taken after consultations with affiliated colleges, many of which reported scheduling conflicts with ongoing campus placement drives. The university has also introduced a provision allowing students with confirmed placement interviews during the exam period to apply for a special reappearance slot. Student union representatives welcomed the move, calling it a long-pending demand. The university added that the revised academic calendar will be uploaded to its website by the end of this week, along with updated guidelines for affiliated colleges.

title: Traffic Police Launch Special Drive Against Illegal Parking Near Sitabuldi Market
body: Nagpur Traffic Police on Thursday launched a special enforcement drive against illegal roadside parking near Sitabuldi's main market area, one of the city's busiest commercial zones. Deputy Commissioner of Police (Traffic) Chinmay Pandit said the drive follows repeated complaints from shopkeepers and commuters about vehicles blocking the main carriageway during peak hours, causing significant congestion. Over 200 vehicles were towed on the first day of the drive, with fines collected exceeding Rs 3 lakh, according to police figures. The department has also proposed designated paid parking zones in coordination with the municipal corporation to provide an alternative for shoppers. Local traders' associations have offered mixed reactions, with some welcoming the decongestion while others expressed concern about the impact on footfall if parking becomes less convenient. The drive is expected to continue through the month, with police signalling similar action in other congested commercial pockets of the city.
